title: Lindiwe's Leather

sentences.text: You are the management accountant at Lindiwe's Leather.
Lindiwe's Leather makes belts and bags in a workshop in Maboneng, Johannesburg.
A belt sells for R450, uses 0.5 m² of leather and has other variable costs of R60.
A bag sells for R1 200, uses 2 m² of leather and has other variable costs of R250.
Leather has cost R180 per m², but from 1 November the supplier charges R200 per m².
A belt needs 0.5 machine hours and a bag 2 machine hours.
Historically, Lindiwe's has sold two belts for every bag.
Because one stitching machine is being repaired, only 700 machine hours are available in November.
Customers will buy at most 600 belts and 300 bags in November.
Fixed costs are R95 000 a month and do not change with the product mix.
A Dubai retailer has asked for 100 bags at R1 000 each, for delivery in November.

required: Calculate how many belts and how many bags Lindiwe's Leather should make in November to earn the most profit, and the profit that results. Use the supplier's new leather price. Ignore the export enquiry in paragraph 3.

recall.question: What kind of business is Lindiwe's Leather?
options: A small maker of leather belts and bags

recall.question: What is your role?
options: A buyer for the Dubai retailer

recall.question: What limits production in November?
options: Machine time, because a machine is being repaired

recall.question: What has changed in the costs?
options: The price of leather has gone up
The units of each product to make, and the profit that results
Breakeven units for belts and bags
A discussion of whether to accept the Dubai order
A total number of units in the usual sales mix
shape.why: Two unit figures (belts and bags) and one profit figure. A combined unit total does not answer it.

options.text: Use the new leather price of R200
Choose the mix that earns the most profit, not the usual sales mix
Use the historical sales mix of two belts per bag
Price the Dubai bags at R1 000

directions.why: 'Earn the most profit' is a decision rule. In June 2026 all three students used the historical sales mix on a question like this.

options: Short-term profit, with machine hours as the limit
lens.why: When one resource is limited, rank the products by contribution per unit of that resource, not per product.

rows.point: Belt contribution R290 (R450 − R100 leather at R200 − R60)
Bag contribution R550 (R1 200 − R400 leather − R250)
Machine hours are the limit: full demand needs 900 hours (600 × 0.5 + 300 × 2) and only 700 are available
Rank by contribution per machine hour: belts R580, bags R275, so make belts first
Make 600 belts (the demand limit), using 300 hours
Use the remaining 400 hours for 200 bags
Profit: R174 000 + R110 000 = R284 000 contribution, less R95 000 fixed costs = R189 000
